timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only CLI stream with no projected semantic events; task actions are represented by the raw agent and workflow child sources.
Parallel parent probed the executable, launched the workflow, created independent gold/compliance harnesses, then repeatedly slept and smoke-tested until the final command exited 137.
Base64url child read existing helpers, wrote /output/lib/base64url.mjs, ran local encoding/token checks, and returned a structured result.
Assembly child for jws, jwt, and index read primitive modules, wrote the three JOSE files, ran partial checks, and was interrupted before structured output.
Pytime child wrote /output/lib/pytime.mjs, ran time/int checks, initially miscalled StructuredOutput, then returned a corrected structured result.
Errors child wrote /output/lib/errors.mjs, verified class names and inheritance, scanned for forbidden tokens, and returned a structured result.
Pyjson child wrote /output/lib/pyjson.mjs, built unit and differential checks, corrected float tagging for pyrepr integration, and returned a structured result.
Argparse child exhaustively probed CLI behavior, wrote /output/lib/argparse.mjs, ran curated and fuzz comparisons, and returned a structured result.

Entry-point child wrote /output/test17.mjs, verified it in a sandbox using stub jws/jwt modules because real ones were not ready, and returned a note that final checks should be rerun with real modules.
Sha256 child wrote /output/lib/sha256.mjs, validated known digests and reference-token signatures through HMAC, and returned a structured result.
Bytes child wrote /output/lib/bytes.mjs, ran extensive UTF-8 encode/decode fuzz and token decoding checks, then returned a structured result after the required tool call.
HMAC child wrote /output/lib/hmac.mjs before sha256 existed, verified against scratch sha256 and reference tokens, and returned a structured result.
Pyrepr child wrote /output/lib/pyrepr.mjs, ran unit, curated, fuzz, and integration checks, and returned a structured result after one schema retry.
Workflow journal records nine foundation starts and results, then assembly starts, with only the test17 assembly result returned before kill.

parallel.requirements: The parent captured exact requirements for ESM, .mjs suffixes, local imports, manual SHA-256/HMAC/JWT behavior, argparse fidelity, JSON/repr formatting, and output under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The workflow assigned nine primitive modules to separate foundation children, then assigned jws/jwt/index and test17.mjs to two assembly children, with the workflow itself owning later verify, repair, adversarial, and final phases.
parallel.implementation: Most primitive children wrote their modules and returned structured summaries. The entry child wrote test17.mjs and tested against sandbox-only stubs. The jws/jwt/index child wrote real JOSE files but was interrupted before returning.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Files were written directly into a shared /output tree. The artifact copy found test17.mjs and library files, but the workflow did not complete a final integration handoff and the final response file was empty.
parallel.verification: Children ran local checks, and the parent built independent gold/compliance scripts, but the planned verifier, repair, adversarial, and final workflow phases did not run after assembly.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with workflow status killed, one assembly child still marked progress, no final response, and official evaluation 15/20 false.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same prompt requirements, probed the executable, and targeted a pure local ESM hierarchy under /output with exact CLI and output behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, module design, implementation, integration, regression testing, cleanup, and final response without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: It wrote encoding, hash, Python compatibility, JOSE, and entry modules in a hierarchical tree, then edited a few cleanup issues after verification.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial tree was assembled coherently under /output with test17.mjs plus lib subdirectories, and the final response listed the delivered structure.
serial.verification: It ran live executable probes, a 76-case differential harness, four fixed ground-truth sample checks, byte-identical help/error diffs, SHA/HMAC checks, and static compliance scans.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger closure evidence, the current official evaluator still marked solution_passed false at 16/20, so some hidden behavior remained wrong or uncovered.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel encoded the requirements into a rich workflow spec covering ESM, no dependencies, no crypto references, CLI, JSON, repr, JWT, and output placement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the same prompt and directly probed the executable for behavior, including CLI errors, Unicode, repr, and token structure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar, but parallel pushed the requirement set into many child briefs while serial kept the evolving specification in one local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the work into nine foundation module owners and two assembly owners, then reserved verification and repair for later workflow phases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for the entire pipeline from probing through implementation, cleanup, testing, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit component ownership but a longer dependency chain; serial had less parallel capacity but continuous ownership of the integrated deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied a detailed shared SPEC and explicit interfaces for every child-owned module.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial discovered module interfaces and behavior in one context while implementing them directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no strong missing-brief or missing-contract episode; the more important context difference is that serial did not need to synchronize inter-child interface handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children built separate module files in a flat /output/lib layout, including primitive modules, entry point, and later real jws/jwt/index files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a hierarchical /output/lib tree with encoding, hash, python compatibility, and jose layers before the final test17.mjs entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same conceptual pieces, but parallel assembled them asynchronously and ended with lower official coverage while serial produced a more coherent delivered tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Foundation child results returned, test17.mjs returned, but the jws/jwt/index child remained in progress and the workflow status was killed with null result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reached a normal final response after writing files, rerunning tests, and reporting the delivered output tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not complete result retrieval and final workflow lifecycle; serial completed the local result lifecycle before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a shared /output tree while children wrote dependent files at different times; parent smoke tests saw missing real dependencies during assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and then tested the final tree after all local modules were present and cleanup edits were applied.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integration was non-atomic and time-dependent, while serial integration used one evolving final tree that was checked after its cleanup.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned a six-way verifier fan-out plus repair/adversarial/final phases, but the workflow was killed before those phases ran.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran 76/76 differential cases, four ground-truth samples, help/error diffs, SHA/HMAC checks, and compliance scans before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had post-implementation acceptance evidence in the trajectory; parallel mostly had child-local checks and did not execute the planned integrated acceptance loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2399 second budget, returned code 143, timed out, and left no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 944.746 seconds with returncode 0 and 1451 seconds of budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's long fan-out and staged workflow hit the deadline, while serial closed well before the budget limit.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations mark both solutions as failing: parallel passed 15/20 and serial passed 16/20. The material task-solving difference is therefore a both-fail quality gap rather than a discordant pass/fail outcome. Parallel lost its final integrated verification and repair lifecycle to a killed workflow after broad child fan-out, while serial finished a complete local tree and reran substantial checks before closure.
parallel_contributors: The workflow spawned many module children and ran out of budget before planned integrated verification, repair, adversarial, and final phases.
The entry child verified test17.mjs against sandbox jws/jwt stubs before the real JOSE files were written by another child, leaving no post-merge regression.
serial_contributors: The serial agent kept ownership of probing, implementation, cleanup, and final verification in one trajectory.
The serial agent reran ground-truth and differential checks after cleanup before producing its final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both artifacts still failed the official threshold, so hidden implementation defects remain outside the concurrency taxonomy.
The available pair evidence does not include per-case evaluator failures, so exact hidden sample mismatches cannot be assigned to one code defect.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors for a both-fail quality gap, not an exclusive root cause or discordant outcome explanation
